text: Management is best defined as the process of
subject: Principles of Management
options: Getting work done through and with people|Working alone to achieve personal goals|Avoiding responsibility for results|Issuing orders without planning
explanation: Management is achieving objectives efficiently and effectively through and with other people.

text: Which function of management involves setting objectives and deciding the course of action in advance
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Planning is deciding in advance what to do how to do it when to do it and who will do it.

text: Management is called a science because it
subject: Principles of Management
options: Has systematised knowledge and principles|Deals only with experiments in labs|Never changes over time|Ignores human behaviour
explanation: Management has an organised body of knowledge and principles which gives it a scientific character.

text: Management is considered an art because it
subject: Principles of Management
options: Requires personal skill and creativity|Is a rigid set of rules|Works only in factories|Eliminates human judgement
explanation: Applying knowledge with personal skill judgement and creativity makes management an art.

text: The three levels of management are top middle and
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Management is divided into top middle and lower (supervisory) levels.

text: Conceptual skills are most important at the top level of management
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Top managers need conceptual skills to see the organisation as a whole and plan long term.

text: State any four functions of management
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Planning organising staffing directing and controlling.
explanation: These five functions form the core of the management process.

text: Distinguish between efficiency and effectiveness in management
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Efficiency is doing things right with minimum waste; effectiveness is doing the right things to achieve goals.
explanation: Efficiency focuses on inputs while effectiveness focuses on achieving the objective.

text: Explain the importance of management in modern organisations
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Management achieves group goals through optimal use of resources reduces costs improves efficiency and coordinates efforts. It helps organisations adapt to a dynamic environment and provides innovation and growth.
explanation: A complete answer should cover goal achievement efficiency coordination adaptation and innovation.

text: F W Taylor is regarded as the father of scientific management
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Taylor pioneered scientific management through time and motion study.

text: Which thinker is associated with the fourteen principles of management
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Henri Fayol proposed fourteen principles of management such as division of work and unity of command.

text: The Hawthorne studies gave rise to which school of management
subject: Principles of Management
options: Human relations school|Scientific management|Bureaucracy school|Systems school
explanation: Elton Mayos Hawthorne experiments highlighted social factors and worker morale.

text: The principle of unity of command means a subordinate should receive orders from
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Unity of command avoids confusion by giving each subordinate a single boss.

text: List any four principles of management given by Fayol
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Division of work authority and responsibility unity of command unity of direction discipline and esprit de corps.
explanation: Any four of Fayols fourteen principles are acceptable.

text: Briefly explain the systems approach to management
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: The systems approach views an organisation as a set of interrelated parts working together to convert inputs into outputs within an environment.
explanation: It stresses interdependence of subsystems and feedback.

text: Describe the contributions of the behavioural school of management
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: The behavioural school shifted attention from rules to people. Elton Mayo showed that social needs morale and informal groups affect output. It led to better leadership motivation and participative management.
explanation: Cover the Hawthorne studies and the emphasis on human relations and motivation.

text: Match the thinker to the idea
subject: Principles of Management
options: Taylor - scientific management|Weber - scientific management|Mayo - bureaucracy|Fayol - systems theory
explanation: Taylor is linked with scientific management while Weber is linked with bureaucracy and Fayol with administrative principles.

text: Every business should have a bureaucracy with clear hierarchy is Weber
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Max Weber described bureaucracy as an ideal organisation based on rules and hierarchy.

text: A plan that is broad and sets the overall direction of an organisation is a
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: A strategy is a long term plan that guides the whole organisation toward its mission.

text: SWOT analysis examines strengths weaknesses opportunities and
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: SWOT stands for strengths weaknesses opportunities and threats.

text: Which of the following is a single use plan
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Budgets and programmes are single use plans while policies and procedures are standing plans.

text: Decision making under certainty means all outcomes of each alternative are known
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Under certainty the manager has complete information about every alternative and its result.

text: List the steps in the planning process
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Setting objectives developing premises identifying alternatives evaluating alternatives selecting a plan and follow up.
explanation: Planning proceeds step by step from objectives to implementation and review.

text: Explain the concept of MBO and its benefits
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Management by Objectives is a process where managers and subordinates jointly set measurable goals and review performance against them. Benefits include clarity of goals motivation participation and better performance appraisal.
explanation: Cover joint goal setting periodic review and the motivational effect of participation.

text: In decision making choosing the first satisfactory alternative rather than the best is called satisficing
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Herbert Simon proposed bounded rationality where managers satisfice instead of optimising.

text: Which decision making technique uses a group of experts who respond anonymously
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: The Delphi technique gathers expert opinion through repeated anonymous questionnaires.

text: Assertion: Planning is the primary function of management. Reason: All other functions depend on plans set in advance
subject: Principles of Management
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: Planning precedes organising staffing directing and controlling so it is primary and the reason explains this.

text: Which term refers to the grouping of activities and the assignment of authority
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Organising involves dividing work into departments and establishing authority relationships.

text: The number of subordinates a manager can effectively supervise is called span of
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Span of control refers to how many people report directly to a manager.

text: Delegation of authority always transfers final responsibility to the subordinate
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Authority can be delegated but ultimate responsibility always remains with the manager.

text: Which structure groups activities by product region or customer
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: A divisional structure creates semi-autonomous units around products or markets.

text: Distinguish between centralisation and decentralisation
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Centralisation concentrates decision making at the top while decentralisation spreads it to lower levels. Neither is absolute and both exist in every organisation.
explanation: The difference is the degree to which lower levels participate in decisions.

text: Explain the principles of delegation of authority
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Delegation involves assigning duties granting authority and creating accountability. Principles include parity of authority and responsibility unity of command and scalar chain. Authority can be delegated but responsibility cannot.
explanation: Cover the three elements of delegation and the key principles that govern it.

text: Assertion: A flat organisation has few levels. Reason: A wide span of control reduces the number of hierarchy levels
subject: Principles of Management
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: A wide span of control means each manager supervises more people so fewer levels are needed.

text: The first step in staffing is
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Staffing begins with estimating manpower needs through human resource planning.

text: The process of choosing the most suitable candidate from applicants is called
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Selection picks the best candidate while recruitment attracts a pool of applicants.

text: Maslow placed self-actualisation at the bottom of his hierarchy of needs
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Physiological needs are at the bottom and self-actualisation is at the top of the hierarchy.

text: Which leadership style allows full participation of subordinates in decisions
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: A democratic leader consults subordinates and encourages participation in decision making.

text: Explain the difference between recruitment and selection
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Recruitment is a positive process that attracts a large pool of candidates. Selection is a negative process that rejects unsuitable applicants and picks the best one.
explanation: Recruitment precedes selection in the staffing sequence.

text: Describe Herzbergs two-factor theory of motivation
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Herzberg divided factors into hygiene factors like salary and working conditions which prevent dissatisfaction and motivators like achievement and recognition which create satisfaction. Hygiene factors do not motivate by themselves.
explanation: Cover the distinction between hygiene factors and motivators and their effect on job satisfaction.

text: Assertion: Directing initiates action. Reason: Directing guides people toward execution of plans
subject: Principles of Management
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: Directing is the executive function that converts plans into action through people.

text: The process of measuring actual performance against standards is called
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Controlling compares actual performance with planned standards and corrects deviations.

text: A standard expressed in money such as sales target or cost limit is a budget
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: A budget is a quantitative standard usually expressed in monetary terms.

text: Controlling that takes place while an activity is in progress is called control
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Concurrent control monitors activities as they happen while feedback control occurs after the event.

text: Which tool of control analyses a project into activities and shows their sequence and timing
subject: Principles of Management
options: PERT and CPM|Ratio analysis|Break even analysis|Budgetary control
explanation: PERT and CPM are network techniques used to plan and control project schedules.

text: Explain the steps in the controlling process
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Establishing standards measuring actual performance comparing performance with standards and taking corrective action.
explanation: These four steps form the control cycle.

text: Why is coordination called the essence of management
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Coordination unites the efforts of all departments toward common goals. It is needed in every function of management so it is not a separate function but the thread that runs through all of them.
explanation: Explain how planning organising staffing directing and controlling each require coordination.

text: A firm sets a standard of ten units per worker per day. A worker produces eight units. The deviation that must be corrected is
subject: Principles of Management
explanation: Deviation equals standard minus actual performance so 10 minus 8 gives 2 units.

text: Read the case: A call centre sets a target of answering calls within twenty seconds. Actual average is forty five seconds and customers complain. Identify the control standard and the corrective action needed
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: The standard is answering calls within twenty seconds. Actual performance of forty five seconds shows a negative deviation. Corrective action includes more staff better training or improved technology to reduce response time.
explanation: Relate the standard to the measured performance and propose realistic corrections.

text: Read the case: A manager notices that output rises whenever he praises workers in team meetings. Using motivation theory explain why recognition improves performance and suggest how to use it
subject: Principles of Management
correctAnswer: Recognition satisfies the esteem need in Maslows hierarchy and acts as a motivator in Herzbergs theory so it raises morale and output. The manager should give regular specific and genuine recognition to sustain motivation.
explanation: Link the observed behaviour to motivation theories and give practical suggestions.
